subject.title: feat(plugin-sdk): generic outbound delivery-report seam; WhatsApp native auto-reply reports provider-accepted sends

question: Should OpenClaw accept `openclaw/plugin-sdk/outbound-delivery-report` as the public contract for self-delivering channel plugins to report canonical sent events?
rationale: This is a new public plugin SDK seam rather than only a private bug fix; automation cannot choose the permanent API name, idempotency contract, and supported caller boundary for maintainers.

options.title: Accept seam after proof
options.body: Require a conflict refresh plus redacted real WhatsApp/runtime proof, then land this seam as the canonical self-delivery report contract.

options.title: Pause for API redesign
options.body: Keep the linked issue open and ask for a narrower or differently named SDK contract before merging any public surface.

options.title: Use channel-local fixes only
options.body: Avoid a generic SDK seam for now and solve WhatsApp or each channel with owner-local sent-hook emitters, accepting more drift risk.

recommendation.title: Accept seam after proof
recommendation.body: Require a conflict refresh plus redacted real WhatsApp/runtime proof, then land this seam as the canonical self-delivery report contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The history signal ties steipete to recent WhatsApp provider-accepted tracking and broad channel/plugin SDK boundary work, which are both central to the API decision.
